verdicts.summary:
Lean uses a different formula here. The display is outline motivation in Section 3.3. The text layer has w_lin and "spatial decay" on p. 12 only, and the page defers the growth-then-decay it illustrates to Lemmas 7.1 and 7.4, so nothing later uses the formula.

The repository has a counterpart for part of it, in another form. `NavierStokes.R3CompactEnergy.energy_balance` (NavierStokes/R3CompactEnergy.lean:186) is the same integration by parts, localized by a compactly supported weight χ. With u = v = u_B and z = ∂ₜw its hypothesis `heq` is L_{u_B}(w, π) = 0 as defined on p. 11. Its conclusion is the χ-weighted identity: weighted `dissipation` and `coupling`, plus three flux terms that carry a derivative of χ. The repository never instantiates it at u = v; its only caller (NavierStokes/R3LocalEnergyEvolution.lean:65) is the difference of two solutions, and the formula is the one the paper writes on p. 123 ("Difference energy", with χ_R).

The unweighted display follows from this by formal steps only when w_lin has spatial support in a fixed compact set for nearby times. Then one takes a cutoff equal to 1 on a ball containing that set (`compact_plateau`, NavierStokes/R3/ComparisonCutoffs.lean:250), and the three flux integrands vanish pointwise. I checked this specialization by hand; no declaration states it.

For a field that decays without compact support, which is what the paper's "sufficient spatial decay" describes, the display needs the three flux terms to tend to zero and the weighted energy, coupling and dissipation to converge as the cutoff exhausts space. I found no declaration stating this:
- The flux statements are inequalities for φ⁸ weights (NavierStokes/R3EnergyBoundary.lean:33, 79; NavierStokes/R3/LocalizedFluxEstimates.lean:90), with no limit statement.
- `localizedEnergy_tendsto` (NavierStokes/R3LocalizedEnergyLimit.lean:77) passes to the limit in the energy only.
- The unweighted whole-space identities (NavierStokes/R3/CompactEnergy.lean:202, 323; NavierStokes/R3/ViscousEnergyBalance.lean:22, 56; NavierStokes/R3/IntegratedDissipation.lean:27) all assume compact support of the velocity and carry a forcing term, not the shear coupling.
- `PeriodicUniqueness.energy_balance` (NavierStokes/PeriodicUniqueness.lean:491) has the display's two right-hand terms without fluxes, but for a periodic difference of two Navier–Stokes solutions on the unit cube.

In the other direction, the Lean identity holds with no decay at all and with independent u and v, so it does not follow from the display either. That rules out lean_weaker as well as lean_stronger.

The skeptic adds that a compactly supported solution of the homogeneous viscous model must vanish by unique continuation, so the formal case would be empty. That is a known kind of result outside the repository; I did not verify it and the ruling does not depend on it.

Severity is low because no later argument of the paper uses the display.
